mission: Arrival at the next survey point, which is not a ruin. The structure has power, a Force-recognition mechanism calibrated for an older era, and a warning message that has been broadcasting on a dead frequency for centuries.
why_now: The bearing lands them on a world that should not carry a functioning Jedi installation. It does. The survey mission now has infrastructure on the other end of it.
conflict: The facility's Force-recognition mechanism scans Ben and grudgingly accepts him — as if it was designed for practitioners whose signature does not quite match his. Something older in his lineage triggers the admit. Desh's instruments say this building should not still be running, and it is.
turning_point: Automated systems wake, cycling a centuries-old warning through dead frequencies until it resolves into archaic Basic: two words, SEAL FAILING.
opening_hook: The structure isn't ruins. It has power.
closing_hook: The message resolves into Basic — archaic but readable. Two words: 'SEAL FAILING.'
emotional_trajectory: Cautious exploration -> growing awe -> sharp alarm

stakes.personal: Ben is standing in front of something the modern Jedi Order does not know exists
stakes.interpersonal: Desh's professional assessment shifts from 'interesting survey find' to 'threat assessment'
stakes.external: An ancient Jedi military installation has been broadcasting a distress signal no one has heard

notes: R02 lands here — the seal exists and is failing. The wrongness and the anomalous ruins converge into a single crisis. Lord Gavran first named — do not over-explain him. The facility does the characterization: what he built, how he organized it, what he kept. Desh's intelligence-operative instinct should read the architecture as military command-and-control; his professional reading carries weight Ben respects. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate what the seal is. He reads the words; the meaning has not reached him yet. Make sure SEAL FAILING lands with weight before Ben is ready to name what it protects against. Rotate the Force-wrongness metaphor for this scene: do not use the handrail or the note-played-flat line; this scene's register is denser pressure, a weight on the chest, not timing or navigation.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Automated systems wake and cycle a centuries-old warning through dead frequencies until it resolves into archaic Basic: SEAL FAILING.
turning_point_detail.shift: The pressure Ben has felt throughout the approach crystallizes from ambient wrongness into a named crisis. The facility is not a ruin; it is a warning beacon. The survey mission now has infrastructure on the other end of it, and that infrastructure is failing.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben is standing in front of something the modern Jedi Order does not know exists. Desh's professional assessment shifts from 'interesting survey find' to 'threat assessment,' and Ben must reckon with the fact that his Order's institutional knowledge has a catastrophic gap.

emotional_arc.start: Cautious exploration — Ben and Desh approach with hands near grips, reading the environment for threat.
emotional_arc.shift: Growing awe — the Force-recognition mechanism's blue pulse and the activation of centuries-dormant systems shift Ben's focus from threat-assessment to comprehension. Something older in his lineage has been recognized by infrastructure he did not know existed.
emotional_arc.end: Sharp alarm — the two-word message lands before Ben is ready to name what it protects against. The weight on his chest tightens into the knowledge that the seal is failing and he is standing in front of the proof.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Desh approach the powered facility on foot across barren terrain, blasters holstered but hands near grips, reading the structure's perimeter for threat.
key_beats.state_change: The abstract wrongness Ben has felt becomes concrete — the facility is not ruins. It has power. It has presence.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's caution sharpens into focused attention. His hand stays near his blaster, but his Force-sense is already reaching toward the structure, trying to read what it is. The wrongness here is denser, a weight on his chest rather than ambient pressure — close and specific, not diffuse.

key_beats.beat_description: The facility's Force-recognition mechanism scans Ben with a blue pulse of light that crawls across his body, lingering as if checking something that does not quite match.
key_beats.state_change: The facility acknowledges Ben. Access is granted, but the mechanism's hesitation — the way the pulse lingers — suggests it was calibrated for a signature that does not quite match his.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben feels the scan like a hand reading his lineage. Something older in him triggers the admit. The wrongness intensifies; the pressure on his chest deepens. Awe begins to displace caution — this is not a threat. This is something that has been waiting.

key_beats.beat_description: Automated systems activate — displays flickering to life, power cells humming louder, a centuries-old warning message cycling through dead frequencies in patterns that do not resolve into language Ben recognizes.
key_beats.state_change: The facility is not dormant. It is waking. The warning has been broadcasting on dead frequencies for centuries, unheard.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's awe crystallizes into focus. He is reading the displays, trying to parse the archaic protocol, aware that Desh is moving — sweeping the entry corridor, sidearm drawn, reading the architecture as military command-and-control. Ben respects that reading. This is not a ruin. This is a command post that has been waiting.

key_beats.beat_description: The warning message resolves into archaic Basic — two words cycling through the dead frequency, clear and unmistakable: SEAL FAILING.
key_beats.state_change: The wrongness, the facility, the centuries-old warning, and the Force-recognition mechanism all converge into a single named crisis. The seal is real. The seal is failing. Ben is standing in front of the proof, and the meaning has not reached him yet — only the weight of the words.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The alarm lands before comprehension. Ben's breath catches. The weight on his chest becomes a pressure that pins him to the moment. He reads the words. He does not yet name what they protect against. The message repeats: SEAL FAILING. SEAL FAILING. The wrongness is not ambient anymore. It is the sound of something breaking.
